deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 14r holds a heavily corrected draft of a business letter and a short shopping list. The only drawing is a decorative looping flourish around a letter (probably 'D') at upper left. Nothing here is a derivation or a calculation.

(a) Top-right memorandum, a list of things to buy:
- 'Regeln u. Wörterverzeichniß für deutsche Rechtschreibung. Clausthal 1855', a spelling guide;
- an item underlined at the head of the list, possibly 'Weber', followed by 'Kalender';
- Oltrogge;
- 'Unterhaltungsschriften ...', entertaining reading;
- stationery: what seems to be 'Tasche', 'Oblaten' (sealing wafers) and 'Dinte' (ink);
- envelopes ('Couvert').

(b) The letter is addressed to a Göttingen bookshop, probably the Dieterich'sche Buchhandlung (the reading 'Dieterich'sche' is a guess). Riemann asks for these books:
1. Oltrogge's 'Sammlung deutscher Lesestücke'. The condition is that it should only be sent if it had not already been ordered since the last Michaelmas, either on account of Pastor Riemann in Quickborn or through Riemann the postal official in Bremen.
   - In an earlier wording he wrote 'my late father' and 'my brother'; he struck these out and substituted the third-person forms.
2. The Clausthal 1855 spelling rules.
3. 'Unterhaltungsschriften für die reifere Jugend', plus a couple of booklets.

The books were to be sent either poste restante to Lehrte, so he could collect them on Sunday the 22nd at 8 a.m. while passing through, or else to Quickborn bei Dannenberg.

The signature reads 'B. Riemann, Dr. phil., Assessor der philos. Facultät', Göttingen; the date is left blank.

Context suggests he was buying schoolbooks for the family home in Quickborn, probably for his sisters, after his father's death. Lehrte is the railway junction on the route from Göttingen and Hannover toward the Elbe region.

Dating, which is my inference and not on the page:
- The 'Clausthal 1855' imprint and the cancelled reference to his late father point to 1855 or later.
- Sunday the 22nd fits April and July 1855.
- July 1855, at the start of the summer vacation, is the most plausible.

The previous page (a record of physics seminar sessions) and the next page (number-theoretic arctangent identities of the form (1/n) = (1/m) + (1/r), with factorizations of n²+1) are unrelated to this letter. The sheet was simply reused.

results.what: Draft letter ordering books and stationery (Oltrogge's reader, Clausthal 1855 orthography rules, juvenile reading) to be sent to Lehrte or Quickborn

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics. It is a personal and administrative letter draft. It is of minor biographical interest only: family matters after his father's death, a journey via Lehrte, and his self-description as 'Assessor der philosophischen Facultät'.

checkable.asserts: 22 July 1855 was a Sunday, consistent with 'Sonntag den 22. d. M.' and a dating to summer 1855
22 April 1855 was also a Sunday, an alternative possible date

transcription_corrections: Top-left pencil note 'Riemann 27' is an archival/later annotation; the line beneath ('Cg. d. Universität Gesuche') is very uncertain and is unlikely to say 'Universität'.

The struck-out passage in the opening paragraph explicitly mentions 'für Rechnung meines seligen Vaters' and 'nach Quickborn bei Dannenberg'. In item 1 the words 'meines seligen Vaters' and 'meinen Bruder' are struck and replaced by 'des Pastors Riemann in Quickborn' and 'den Postsecretär Riemann in Bremen' ('Postsecretär' is a probable reading).
'Dieterich'sche' Hofbuchhandlung is a plausible but uncertain reading of the addressee.
'der Ansicht' in the list and in item 3 is uncertain and possibly something else entirely; the line reads 'Unterhaltungsschriften für die reifere Jugend ...'.
'Mündschd.' is unreadable as transcribed; the item is stationery (paper, envelopes).
